findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert (TOCTOU)
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts in separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit can be exceeded. It also issues a COUNT query on every uncached tag when a limit is set.

findings.title: Cache entry set before the DB write, so a rejected device is cached as tagged
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (or any DB error), the key stays cached for 29 minutes. The next request from that device then returns nil and is silently allowed through. The limit is therefore enforced only on the first request per device per cache window, and transient DB errors also cause skipped tagging.

findings.title: Tagging moved from an async goroutine to the synchronous auth path
findings.body: TagDevice, which does DB reads and writes, now runs inline in Authenticate. Every anonymous request that misses the cache pays that latency. A slow or failing database now delays or blocks anonymous page loads, which previously completed independently of tagging. The request context is also now used, so a client cancellation aborts the tagging.

findings.title: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update
findings.body: A zero-row update does not necessarily mean the limit was reached for a new device. It can also happen for a device last updated more than 30 days ago or just outside the time window. A returning-but-expired device is rejected, and Authenticate then fails with a generic error rather than a clear limit message.

findings.title: Limit test covers only the rejection of a new device
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit checks only that a second new device is rejected. It does not check that an existing device can still update at the limit, that the limit=0 path is unlimited, or the client.go behaviour of returning the error. impl_test and the client tests were not extended.
